abstract:
In the relentless pursuit of longevity and vitality, the scientific community has increasingly turned its attention to natural compounds that can activate the body’s inherent anti-aging pathways. Among these, resveratrol and sirtuins have emerged as pivotal players, offering promising avenues for enhancing human health and longevity. Resveratrol, a polyphenolic compound found in various plants, including grape skins, raspberries, mulberries, pomegranates, and raw cacao, has garnered significant attention for its potential to mimic the benefits of caloric restriction, a well-known longevity-promoting strategy. This compound belongs to a family of molecules known as polyphenols, which are renowned for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. The mechanism by which resveratrol exerts its effects is intriguingly linked to the activation of sirtuins, a group of proteins that play a crucial role in regulating cellular health and longevity.
